item.title: Xi meets Togo's president of Council of Ministers, elevating bilateral ties to community with shared future for new era
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-14
Xi meets Togo's president of Council of Ministers, elevating bilateral ties to community with shared future for new era Chinese President Xi Jinping meets with President of the Council of Ministers of Togo Faure Essozimna Gnassingbé, who is on an official visit to China, at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, capital of China, Oct. 13, 2026. (Xinhua/Li Xiang) BEIJING, Oct. 13 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping met with President of the Council of Ministers of Togo Faure Essozimna Gnassingbé in Beijing on Tuesday, during which the two leaders announced the elevation of bilateral relations to a China-Togo community with a shared future for the new era. Xi pointed out that the traditional China-Togo friendship was personally forged by leaders of an older generation of both countries, enjoying a solid foundation and growing ever stronger with the passage of time. China and Togo share aligned visions for friendly cooperation and enjoy broad prospects ahead, Xi said. Xi called on the two sides to further enhance exchanges at all levels between the two parties and the two countries, deepen the sharing of experiences in governance, and firmly support each other on issues concerning core interests and major concerns. China welcomes Togo to effectively utilize measures such as China's zero-tariff policy and the "green channel" for products exported to China, further enhance its role as a regional hub for trade and logistics, and facilitate the entry of more distinctive local and regional products into the Chinese market, Xi added. Xi noted that China appreciates Togo's efforts to expand the cross-border use of the RMB and is willing to strengthen cooperation with Togo in new energy, digital intelligence and other fields to support Togo's industrialization process. Noting that China and Togo share similar positions on international and regional affairs, Xi also called on the two sides to enhance multilateral coordination. Xi put forward four principles for the constructive participation of all parties in the settlement of hotspot issues in Africa. First, adhering to the principle of "Africa-led." The African people are the true masters of Africa and should play a central role in regional affairs, Xi said. Second, upholding fairness and justice. All participating parties should abide by the purposes and principles of the United Nations Charter and respect the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the countries concerned, he noted. Third, promoting ceasing hostilities for peace. Wars and unilateral sanctions cannot fundamentally resolve conflicts between countries. It is imperative to uphold mutual respect, conduct extensive consultations, seek common ground while shelving differences, and practice mutual understanding and accommodation. Fourth, addressing both symptoms and root causes. Efforts should focus on immediate security while planning for long-term development, Xi said. Faure, who is on an official visit to China, said that during his visit, he personally witnessed the remarkable achievements of Chinese modernization and the extensive promotion of fine traditional Chinese culture under the leadership of President Xi, and gained a deeper understanding of China's governance philosophy and the key to success. Noting that next year marks the 55th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations between the two countries, he said Togo is willing to enhance mutual trust with China, strengthen dialogue and communication, deepen enduring and mutually beneficial cooperation to jointly build a Togo-China community with a shared future for the new era, and better benefit the two peoples. The Togolese side fully agrees with the important principles proposed by President Xi for the constructive participation of all parties in the settlement of hotspot issues in Africa, Faure said. He expressed Togolese appreciation for China on its significant role in maintaining world peace and stability and jointly addressing global challenges, as well as the willingness to strengthen multilateral cooperation with China, jointly uphold multilateralism, and safeguard the interests of developing countries. item.title: China, Botswana establish comprehensive strategic cooperative partnership
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-14
China, Botswana establish comprehensive strategic cooperative partnership Chinese President Xi Jinping and his wife Peng Liyuan hold a welcome ceremony for Botswana's President Duma Gideon Boko and his wife Kaone Boko in the Northern Hall of the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, capital of China, Oct. 13, 2026. Xi held talks with Boko, who is on a state visit to China, after the welcome ceremony in Beijing on Tuesday. (Xinhua/Xie Huanchi) BEIJING, Oct. 13 (Xinhua) -- During their talks in Beijing on Tuesday, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Botswana's President Duma Gideon Boko announced the elevation of bilateral relations to a comprehensive strategic cooperative partnership. Noting that this year marks the 105th anniversary of the founding of the Communist Party of China and the 60th anniversary of Botswana's independence, Xi said the two countries' ruling parties should strengthen cooperation and deepen exchanges on governance experience. China supports Botswana in pursuing a development path suited to its national conditions, Xi said. He called on both sides to further improve the framework for economic and trade cooperation, and tap into new opportunities created by China's zero-tariff policy for African countries that have diplomatic ties with China. China is ready to strengthen cooperation with Botswana in the digital economy, agriculture, animal husbandry and other sectors, and to carry out the smart education project, Xi added. On promoting China-Botswana and China-Africa mining cooperation, Xi said Africa's resources belong to Africa, and this is the premise for cooperation. China is willing to share its own experience and help African countries formulate mining development plans tailored to their national conditions, and China will encourage Chinese enterprises to transfer green technologies suited to African conditions, Xi said. He said China will continue to promote China-Africa mining cooperation to move up the value chain and explore affordable, sustainable and innovative financing models. Noting that Africa's resources should not become a tool for geopolitical rivalry, Xi said China welcomes all parties' genuine contributions to Africa's development and stands ready to work with Africa to create a more enabling environment for investment and business operations. China has lifted all its poor population out of poverty and forged a successful development path with Chinese characteristics, from which Botswana has much to learn, Boko noted. He said that Botswana highly values its ties with China, and will firmly adhere to the one-China principle and oppose any separatist moves toward "Taiwan independence" and any external interference in China's internal affairs. Botswana is willing to strengthen development strategy alignment with China and welcomes more Chinese enterprises to invest and do business in Botswana, said Boko. He added that the country stands ready to maintain close coordination and cooperation with China, uphold multilateralism, strengthen the solidarity of developing countries, promote Africa-China solidarity and cooperation, and make the global governance system more inclusive and representative. After their talks, the two heads of state jointly witnessed the signing of multiple cooperation documents covering such areas as implementing the Global Security Initiative, Belt and Road cooperation, green minerals, health, and human resources. During Boko's state visit to China, the two sides issued a joint statement on establishing a China-Botswana comprehensive strategic cooperative partnership. Prior to the talks, Xi and his wife Peng Liyuan held a welcome ceremony for Boko and his wife Kaone Boko in the Great Hall of the People. Xi and Peng also held a welcome banquet for them in the evening. item.title: A continuously innovating China is a land of opportunity
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-13
A continuously innovating China is a land of opportunity A customer tries out a new-generation tri-fold smartphone by Chinese tech firm Huawei, the Mate XT 2, at a Huawei store in Hangzhou, east China's Zhejiang province, Sept. 7, 2026. (Photo/Long Wei) Chinese brands are increasingly capturing global attention in the consumer electronics sector. Early this September, they took center stage at IFA Berlin, the world's leading consumer electronics trade show. On display were Chinese humanoid robots advancing into real-world application scenarios and smart home products featuring proactive sensing and collaborative AI services. Not long ago, the smartphone industry saw a "super release week" for foldable phones. Huawei, Xiaomi, and Apple unveiled their respective flagship products within 72 hours, putting leading Chinese and international brands against each other in the same product category and sparking widespread discussion. Such moments are no longer outliers; they reflect a broader industrial shift. Decades ago, China's manufacturing base was comparatively underdeveloped. Across many sectors, the country started late, trailing global leaders in advanced technologies, standard-setting influence, and even foundational design concepts. Its early path forward relied heavily on imitation and incremental improvement. Today, that narrative has reversed. From artificial intelligence and new energy vehicles to robotics and aerospace reusability, China now competes on equal footing -- or leads -- in numerous domains. In previously uncharted territories, it has emerged as both a pioneer and a rule-maker. These breakthroughs stem from the cumulative power of scientific and technological innovation. Take the smartphone industry as an example. Ultimately, it is exclusive cutting-edge technologies that have empowered Chinese brands to march into the high-end market. Breaking free from the lower rungs of industrial and value chains represents an arduous uphill growth, as well as the continuous forging of brand competitiveness and technological "moats." None of this would have been possible without a highly coordinated innovation ecosystem. The numbers tell a clear story. The World Intellectual Property Organization recently released its report on the world's top 100 innovation clusters as part of the Global Innovation Index 2026. China, with 25 of the world's top 100 innovation clusters, maintained its position as the economy with the largest number of listed clusters for the fourth consecutive year. The Shenzhen-Hong Kong-Guangzhou cluster ranked first for the second consecutive year. As a cornerstone of China's national innovation ecosystem, the vigorous development of these regional innovation clusters mirrors the steady rise of the country's sci-tech innovation strength. Progress is driven by clear strategic priorities: state support for sci-tech advancement, the cultivation of advanced, locally adapted industrial capabilities, and targeted policy incentives. A robot dances with residents in Taoyuan subdistrict, Shawan, northwest China's Xinjiang Uygur autonomous region. (Photo/Yang Wenxiu) Equally important is the sheer scale and dynamism of the country's domestic market, which generates rich application scenarios for iterative testing and commercialization. Underpinning both is a deepening talent pool, fueled by tighter integration across education, research, and industry -- a virtuous cycle that continually upgrades the quality and distribution of skilled professionals. All these efforts to enrich the soil nurture the seeds of innovation and creativity, unleashing the momentum of high-quality development. Yet a clearer understanding of how China's innovation-driven model works also makes it harder to sustain certain misconceptions. For some time, politicians and media in some countries have been keen on hyping the so-called "China Shock 2.0", attributing China's progress in high-end manufacturing to industrial subsidies, and thereby stoking anxiety. In practice, as one international observer noted, China operates like "the world's toughest gym." Competition and innovation are embedded in its development model. Rooted in innovation, China's development brings the world not a "shock" but opportunity, not a "squeeze" but empowerment. A technician conducts tests on new materials at a research institute of storage materials in Meishan, southwest China's Sichuan province. (Photo/Pan Shuai) The evidence is mounting. Volkswagen has adjusted its R&D plans at its headquarters in Wolfsburg based on the model of its R&D center in Hefei, east China's Anhui province. Chinese AI models have ranked first for 20 consecutive weeks in terms of weekly global usage among large AI models. As a new round of scientific and technological revolution and industrial transformation converges with China's historic transition in its development model, China is pressing ahead with innovation and working to build itself into a global source of scientific and technological innovation. With such fertile ground for development, China is set to continue surprising the world with innovation. Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. All Rights Reserved.

item.title: China leverages electric vehicles to stabilize the power grid
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-13
China leverages electric vehicles to stabilize the power grid International buyers are introduced to an ultra-fast-charging battery for new energy vehicles at the 2026 Power Battery Application Ecosystem Exhibition in Yibin, southwest China's Sichuan province, Sept. 3, 2026. (Photo/Lan Feng) A global energy revolution is underway, centered on replacing fossil fuels with renewable energy and gasoline and diesel vehicles with electric vehicles (EVs). China is spearheading this shift, and developing a new power system integrating source, grid, load, and storage is an inevitable path forward. As the stock of new energy vehicles climbs toward the 100-million mark, massive numbers of EVs will transcend their traditional role as transportation tools. They are emerging as a critical component of the next-generation power infrastructure. China is expected to have 110 million to 160 million EVs on the road by 2030, with the number projected to rise to 300 million to 400 million by 2040. As ultra-fast charging networks expand, the strain of synchronized charging on local grids is becoming increasingly apparent. For instance, if 5 million EVs were to charge simultaneously overnight at 10 kW each, the resulting demand -- 50 million kW -- would far exceed the peak capacity of most municipal grids. Shifting EV charging from unmanaged, decentralized charging to coordinated, bidirectional energy flow, is therefore crucial. The key lies in enabling vehicle-to-grid (V2G) technology, which allows EVs to interact dynamically with the power network. At its core, V2G transforms EVs from passive grid consumers into active, mobile energy storage units. Vehicles can draw power during off-peak hours and feed electricity back into the grid during periods of high demand. This not only alleviates grid congestion but also creates new revenue streams for owners who participate in wholesale energy markets. With an average 70-kWh battery pack, leveraging surplus cycling capacity for grid services could generate cumulative lifetime returns of 15,000 to 75,000 yuan ($2,240 to $11,198). In effect, EVs are shifting from depreciating consumer products to income-generating assets. A worker inspects charging piles for electric vehicles in a workshop of a new energy company in Luoyang, central China's Henan province. (Photo/Zhang Yixi) Battery life and safety are among the public's major concerns. Research shows that properly managed V2G operations do not accelerate battery degradation; on the contrary, they can help extend battery calendar life. Current lithium iron phosphate (LFP) batteries used in EVs can undergo about 3,000 full charge-discharge cycles before their capacity falls to 70 percent. Yet a typical household vehicle consumes only about 500 cycles over 10 to 15 years of use, leaving substantial capacity for additional applications. Technologies such as bidirectional pulsing can achieve more uniform lithium distribution, suppress lithium plating, and boost fast-charging and low-temperature performance. Meanwhile, V2G operation keeps batteries mostly at a partial state of charge. This prevents calendar-life degradation caused by long-term storage at full charge. When paired with intelligent risk monitoring, these systems effectively minimize safety incidents. V2G applications have already taken shape in three typical scenarios. The first is the "point" scenario in industrial parks, where vehicle batteries operate in coordination with photovoltaic generation and energy storage facilities. The second is the "line" scenario in transportation, where integrated solar-storage-charging systems and batteries used for swapping at heavy-truck stations can supply power to passenger vehicles, reducing the impact on the main power grid. The third is the "area" scenario in buildings, where integrated "home-vehicle-grid" systems enable comprehensive management of building energy use and V2G operations. Looking ahead, V2G is expected to become a major form of distributed short-duration energy storage in China. Given that high-rise buildings dominate China's urban landscape and that conditions for installing fixed energy storage systems at home are limited, using EVs parked in underground garages for energy storage is a more practical option. Electric vehicles are charged in Qingzhou, east China's Shandong province. (Photo/Wang Jilin) Under China's 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030) for the development of the new type of power system, the aggregate adjustable charging capacity enabled by V2G is expected to reach 50 million kilowatts by 2030. By 2040, as the growth of fixed energy storage slows, V2G energy storage capacity could exceed 4 billion kilowatt-hours. Conservatively estimated, the total battery capacity of 350 million EVs will reach 25 billion kilowatt-hours by 2050, enough to meet the country's electricity demand for one day in an emergency. The next five years will be a launch phase for the V2G industry. As technical standards are improved, market mechanisms are put in place and business models mature, more than 100 million EVs will effectively form a vast network of "mobile power banks" for the grid, providing strong support for energy transition. (Ouyang Minggao is an academician of the Chinese Academy of Sciences and a professor at Tsinghua University. The article was compiled by People's Daily journalist Wang Zheng.) item.title: Commentary: China's health approach advances wellbeing of humanity
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-13
Commentary: China's health approach advances wellbeing of humanity BEIJING, Oct. 13 (Xinhua) -- For a country of over 1.4 billion people, ensuring the health of its population is not merely a domestic priority, but also an important contribution to humanity. Since the 18th National Congress of the Communist Party of China (CPC) in 2012, China has further stepped up efforts in ensuring people's health, setting out the guiding principles for health work in the new era and making major decisions and arrangements for fully advancing the Healthy China Initiative. This has delivered historic achievements in the country's health sector and laid a solid health foundation for national rejuvenation. A series of facts and figures shows the profound changes in health. China has put in place the world's largest systems for medical services, traditional medicine, disease prevention and control, and healthcare security. Its health services have seen steady progress in capacity, accessibility and equity, alongside continuous improvements in people's health. China withstood the severe impact of the global COVID-19 pandemic -- a remarkable feat for a populous nation like China. The development of health services has brought concrete benefits to the Chinese people. So far, China has more than 1.1 million medical and health institutions. Over 90 percent of people in China can reach their nearest medical service facilities within 15 minutes. Its basic medical insurance covers around 95 percent of the population. In 2025, the average life expectancy in China reached 79.25 years. The infant mortality rate fell to 3.8 per 1,000 and the maternal mortality rate dropped to 13.4 per 100,000, making China one of the high-performing countries in maternal and child health recognized by the World Health Organization. China's approach to promoting people's health epitomizes the country's people-centered development philosophy. Through consistent efforts in medical and healthcare system reforms, capacity-building, legislation and health promotion, among others, China has blazed a path of inclusive and balanced health development to ensure health for all -- a solemn promise of the CPC and the Chinese government. Undoubtedly, China's all-round progress in its medical and health sector marks an important contribution to the sustainable development of humanity. As the world faces various health challenges, China has actively engaged in global health governance. China has deepened cooperation with other countries in the medical and health sector, worked together to address cross-border public health risks, solidly advanced the building of a community of health for all, contributing China's strength to the global health cause. Traditional Chinese medicine has been introduced to more than 190 countries and regions. Since late 2012, China has dispatched medical aid teams to 59 countries and regions. During the COVID-19 pandemic, China supplied a multitude of anti-epidemic products to the world. People's health is an important indicator of socialist modernization. With clear goals and intensified efforts, China will unswervingly follow the path of health development with Chinese characteristics and advance the Healthy China Initiative to secure greater progress in enhancing people's health. As a major country, China will also further participate in global health cooperation and governance to contribute more to the wellbeing of humanity. Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. All Rights Reserved.

item.title: World's largest ice and snow theme park to expand to record size this winter
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-13
World's largest ice and snow theme park to expand to record size this winter People visit the Harbin Ice-Snow World, the world's largest ice-and-snow theme park, in Harbin, northeast China's Heilongjiang Province, Jan. 27, 2026. (Xinhua/Wang Song) HARBIN, Oct. 13 (Xinhua) -- Harbin Ice-Snow World in northeast China -- the world's largest ice-and-snow theme park -- will set a new record this winter by expanding its site to 1.25 million square meters, with a total of 400,000 cubic meters of ice and snow used. The announcement was made on Monday at the opening ceremony of the 2026-2027 ice-and-snow season promotion event, held by the Heilongjiang provincial ice-and-snow tourism development promotion association. In February this year, the globally renowned winter attraction in Harbin, Heilongjiang's provincial capital, received more than 120,000 visitors in a single day, a historic high, winning praise from domestic and international tourists. The park is expected to feature more than 1,000 ice-and-snow structures this winter, with six major sections covering ice-and-snow landscapes, amusement experiences, performances, ice-and-snow competitions, themed IP and supporting services, offering an immersive winter experience. Core landmarks such as the park gate and main tower will be upgraded. The visitor experience and performances will also be improved. "Key landscapes will be renewed, and there will be more interactive experiences," said Sun Zemin, a promoter of Harbin Ice-Snow World. In deepening the integration of sports and tourism, Harbin Ice-Snow World will work with Harbin municipal sports bureau to host a series of ice-and-snow sports events, covering curling and ice hockey among others, to promote winter sports. The theme park is now in full preparation for the 2026-2027 ice-and-snow season. China has unveiled an ambitious plan to develop its ice and snow economy as a new economic driver, targeting a total market size of 1.2 trillion yuan (about 178.3 billion U.S. dollars) by 2027 and 1.5 trillion yuan by 2030, according to a guideline released by the State Council in 2024. Leveraging the opportunity, Harbin is implementing a slew of market regulation and tourist guidance measures to continue optimizing its tourism experience, adding greater economic momentum through the use of its ice and snow resources. item.title: Shanghai wins 1st WIPO City of Innovation award
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-13
Shanghai wins 1st WIPO City of Innovation award WIPO Director General Daren Tang (L) presents an award to Chinese city Shanghai during the Inaugural Award Ceremony for the first WIPO City of Innovation award at the headquarters of the WIPO in Geneva, Switzerland, Oct. 12, 2026. Chinese city Shanghai, Britain's Liverpool and Belgium's Charleroi were announced Monday by the World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO) as winners of the first WIPO City of Innovation award. (Xinhua/Lian Yi) GENEVA, Oct. 12 (Xinhua) -- Chinese city Shanghai, Britain's Liverpool and Belgium's Charleroi were announced Monday by the World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO) as winners of the first WIPO City of Innovation award. Launched for the first time in 2026, the WIPO City of Innovation award is open to cities across all 194 WIPO member states and is bestowed on visionary cities for their bold pledges to foster innovation and creativity over the coming year. The three winners were chosen from 15 finalist cities. According to WIPO, Shanghai's vision is to strengthen its position as an international hub for science, technology and intellectual property (IP), while fostering a broader culture of innovation and creativity. Its pledges include expanding IP education and services, opening innovation infrastructure and data, supporting cultural and creative industries, and strengthening connections between research, industry, entrepreneurs and investors. Zhou Yaming, Deputy Secretary-General of the Shanghai Municipal People's Government, said the award represents WIPO's strong recognition of Shanghai's innovative developments and its efforts in building a thriving IP ecosystem. "It also reflects the international community's endorsement of China's commitment to open innovation, mutual benefits and shared success," He said. Winners were selected by an independent international jury of high-profile experts in the cultural and creative sectors, urban planning, community development, and innovation-driven growth. Andrea Dempster Chung, member of the International Jury Panel and Co-Founder & Executive Director for Kingston Creative, said Shanghai's application was extremely impressive, not just because of its strong research and development base that the city already had, but for the sheer scale of its ambitions and the strength of pledges. "This would be pivotal in shifting the city's future and this is one of the reasons why Shanghai was selected," she said. item.title: China rolls out "token factories" to drive AI economy
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-13
China rolls out "token factories" to drive AI economy This photo provided by iSoftStone Information Technology (Group) Co., Ltd. shows a scene inside a token factory at the Beijing Economic-Technological Development Area in Beijing, capital of China, Sept. 21, 2026. (Xinhua) BEIJING, Oct. 12 (Xinhua) -- As AI applications gain momentum, China is accelerating the rollout of "token factories" in a bid to build an economic order suited to the AI era. Every time a user prompts an AI model to generate code, images or video, tokens are consumed behind the scenes. In March, China adopted "ciyuan" as the official Chinese term for "token," giving its AI services a standard unit for measuring, settling and tracking usage -- similar to how electricity is measured in kilowatt-hours. In late September, Beijing unveiled an action plan to accelerate the development of the token economy for 2026-2028. "This is the first provincial-level policy in China specifically dedicated to the token economy," said Zhang Jinrui, an official with the Beijing Municipal Bureau of Economy and Information Technology. "With the rollout of Beijing's new policy, tokens are no longer just a technical term associated with large models. The token economy has officially entered a stage of industrial application and institutional development," said Liu Yong, president of the Beijing-based Zhongguancun Internet Finance Institute. The Beijing action plan calls for building world-class token factories and establishing tiered evaluation standards, with throughput capacity, time to first token, PUE (power usage effectiveness) and cache hit rate as core metrics, to ensure the large-scale supply of high-quality tokens. A token factory can be thought of as the AI era's equivalent of a power plant. It integrates electricity, chips, data and models to directly produce tokens. Unlike traditional data centers that only rent out computing cards, customers no longer need to deploy models or optimize inference themselves -- they simply pay for the tokens they use. In the Beijing Economic-Technological Development Area, the Chinese capital's first token factory is now in operation, with a daily capacity of up to 1.4 trillion tokens in its first phase. The plan also designates token distribution platforms as part of the city's new infrastructure layout, exploring market-based pricing and circulation mechanisms for tokens, so that tokens can truly be measured and traded as an economic factor. On the application side, the new policy encourages the development of general-purpose and industry-specific AI agents, bringing token capabilities into sectors such as industry, research and government affairs. Chen Guangming, an official with the Beijing Municipal Bureau of Economy and Information Technology, said token consumption is currently growing fastest in AI-generated content and programming, and more vertical industries will become potential growth drivers for token consumption in the future. "In the internet era, competition was all about traffic and user attention. In the AI era, the logic has shifted -- what matters now is the quality and efficiency of outputting effective tokens," Liu said, adding that the shift from a traffic economy -- one built on user visits and attention -- to a token economy represents a new trend in China's economic development. Data from China's National Data Administration shows that by June, the country's average daily token calls had surpassed 500 trillion. "More than half of those calls were made in Beijing," Zhang said, noting that the city has so far registered 242 large models for public use. Beijing's early push is aimed not merely at building a series of token factories, but at exploring institutional rules suited to the token economy, making the city a testing ground for the industry's development, according to local authorities. Elsewhere, localities across China are developing token economies tailored to their own strengths, as part of efforts to implement the State Council's guidelines on the "AI Plus" initiative. The guidelines aim to build a systematic support framework for AI covering models, data, computing power, applications, open-source development, talent, policies and regulations, and security. In May, north China's Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region, drawing on its green computing resources, launched a token trading platform integrating model calls, token matching and transaction settlement. Nanning, capital of south China's Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, is exploring new models such as cross-border data compliance and remote model inference delivery, helping domestic computing power and large-model capabilities reach ASEAN markets as standardized token services. East China's Anhui Province, meanwhile, encourages banks to offer "token loans" as a financial tool for the token economy. Industry observers generally agree that the global token economy remains in its early stage but holds vast potential. A research report by CICC, a Chinese investment bank, sees "token factories" as one of the fastest-growing and most commercially promising business models for large-model developers in the near term. JPMorgan predicts that China's AI inference token consumption will grow about 370-fold between 2025 and 2030. China's three major telecom operators rolled out token packages in May for individual users as well as government and enterprise clients, bringing token commercialization further into reach for individual consumers. Li Lingran, an engineer at an internet company in Beijing, says using large AI models at work has become as essential as water. He now spends more than 200 yuan (about 30 U.S. dollars) a month on tokens, even more than his traditional mobile phone bill. "This is a shift you can't ignore," he said. item.title: Xi calls for decisive progress in Healthy China advancement
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-13
Xi calls for decisive progress in Healthy China advancement Chinese President Xi Jinping, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, delivers an important speech during a national meeting on health in Beijing, capital of China. The meeting was held in Beijing on Monday and Tuesday. (Xinhua/Xie Huanchi) BEIJING, Oct. 13 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping has called for efforts to firmly follow a path with Chinese characteristics in developing the country's health programs, to secure decisive progress in the Healthy China Initiative over the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030). Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, made the remarks at a national meeting on health held in Beijing on Monday and Tuesday. Xi stressed that people's health is a key benchmark of a nation's prosperity and strength. Since the 18th CPC National Congress in 2012, the Party has made a major decision to launch the Healthy China Initiative, promoting the establishment of the world's largest systems of medical services, traditional medicine, disease prevention and control, and healthcare security, said Xi, noting that the country has achieved historic accomplishments and made all-round progress in healthcare. In 2025, China's average life expectancy rose to 79.25 years, while its major health indicators remained at the leading position among upper-middle-income countries and countries with a population exceeding 100 million. Xi said the goal is to build a Healthy China, where health services are ensured in a balanced, inclusive, high-quality and efficient manner. Xi stressed that people's health should be factored into all policies and reflected in every aspect of work. Prevention, he said, is the most cost-effective and efficient approach to protecting public health. He called for greater emphasis on foundational health work, addressing risks at their source, and encouraging the public to adopt a sound understanding of health and take an active role in managing their own well-being. He also called for a stronger disease prevention and control system to guard against large-scale outbreaks. Xi underscored the need to optimize the functions and structural layout of medical institutions so that people can access medical care close to home and receive effective treatment. China has supported the development of 125 regional medical centers in areas where high-quality medical resources are relatively scarce. Notably, more than 90 percent of residents can access nearby medical and healthcare services within 15 minutes, while primary-level medical institutions account for over 50 percent of all medical visits nationwide. He also urged efforts to improve mechanisms for the preservation and innovative development of traditional Chinese medicine, strengthen basic research and original innovation in the health sector, and enhance the patient experience. Xi stressed that coordinating the development and regulation of medical services, medical insurance, and pharmaceuticals should be a key priority in reforming China's medical and healthcare systems. He also called for efforts to train and develop a sufficient number of highly qualified medical professionals. Efforts will also be made to actively promote the building of a global community of health for all, work with other countries to address major challenges in the health sector, and continuously improve the health and well-being of people around the world, he said. Other Chinese leaders Li Qiang, Zhao Leji, Wang Huning, Cai Qi, Ding Xuexiang and Li Xi attended the event. In his concluding remarks, Li Qiang said Xi's important speech provided guidance for advancing China's health sector. Li called for better coordination between improvements in public health and economic and social development, and urged deeper reform, innovation, opening up and cooperation, stronger prevention and control of major diseases, further development of a tiered diagnosis and treatment system, and greater use of science and technology to improve health services.
